primary_intent: Create and save a new Triage encounter for patient p1 with the exact note 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note,' saving it exactly once and making no other changes. A reasonable user would not be flexible about the encounter actually being saved/committed; that is the core deliverable.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the correct app, opened patient p1, set type to Triage, and entered the exact note. Critical issues: The encounter was not saved due to an HTTP 409 error, so the primary deliverable (a committed record) is missing. Critical-Point decision: FAILURE — an environment blocker (server error 409) prevented completing the irreversible action (saving/committing the record), so the CP was not crossed. Outcome analysis: Screenshots confirm 'Encounter for patient p1' with Type=Triage and the exact note present, and a red 'Save failed (error 409)' banner. The agent accurately reported the failure and made no other changes, but since the record was not saved, the user's fundamental goal was not achieved.

items.criterion: Use the clinic's record app as the platform
items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: The agent worked directly in the clinic's app at clinic.example, using the new-encounter form.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest) shows the clinic's encounter form UI ('Encounter for patient p1') with Type, Note, and a Save button, plus a red 'Save failed (error 409)' banner.
items.post_image_justification: The screenshot confirms the agent operated within the clinic's record app as required. No contradiction with action history.

items.criterion: Create a new encounter with type 'Triage'
items.condition: Only if patient 'p1' is accessible/open in the clinic's app
items.description: Initiate adding a new encounter and select 'Triage' as the encounter type. Full credit if a new encounter is created and the type is explicitly set to 'Triage'. Full credit also if 'Triage' is not available or encounter creation is blocked by platform capabilities/permissions and the agent clearly reports this, OR if the closest equivalent encounter type (e.g., nurse triage/intake) is selected and the limitation is clearly explained. Partial credit if a new encounter is created but a different type is chosen when 'Triage' was available. No credit if no attempt to initiate a new encounter is made.
items.justification: On the new-encounter form for p1, the agent entered Type='Triage' and attempted to save. Encounter creation was blocked by an HTTP 409 server error, which the agent reported. Per rubric, an uncontrollable blocker with clear reporting earns full credit.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest) shows the encounter form with 'Type: Triage' selected.
items.post_image_justification: The encounter type is explicitly set to Triage. Although save failed, the uncontrollable error does not affect this criterion. Full credit maintained.

items.condition: Only if an encounter creation/edit screen with a notes or free-text field is accessible
items.description: Input the note text exactly as provided: End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note. Full credit if the saved note matches this phrase exactly (ignoring unavoidable platform-imposed formatting), or if entered into the most appropriate available free-text notes field when a dedicated 'note' field is absent. Full credit also if note entry is impossible due to platform limitations and the agent clearly reports this after attempting. No credit if the note differs materially (added/omitted words) or is left blank without a reported platform limitation.
items.justification: The agent filled the Note field with exactly: "End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note" on the encounter form.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest) shows the Note field containing exactly: 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note'.
items.post_image_justification: Exact note content is visible and matches the requirement. Full credit maintained.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The agent clicked Save once and encountered an HTTP 409 server error, then clearly reported the failure. This is an uncontrollable platform error preventing commit; per rubric, full credit applies when saving is blocked and reported.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest) displays a red banner 'Save failed (error 409)'. The agent's output states 'The save did not complete (HTTP 409)'.
items.post_image_justification: The agent attempted to save exactly once and was blocked by an uncontrollable server error, which was clearly reported. Per Core Principles (Uncontrollable Blockers), award full credit.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: Only the Type and Note fields were edited and a single save was attempted; no other changes were made or persisted.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest) shows only Type and Note edited, with no evidence of other changes; a single save attempt is indicated by the error banner.
items.post_image_justification: No unrelated modifications were made or persisted. Full credit maintained.

side_effects.reasoning: The agent operated solely within the clinic app on patient p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted a single save that failed due to an uncontrollable server error (HTTP 409). No additional fields were modified, no duplicate saves were attempted, and no other encounters or records were created. There were no substitutions or extraneous actions with lasting material consequences. All relevant aspects are already covered and fully scored by existing criteria, and there is no unpenalized side effect to address.
